title: The Geography of Human Behavior
content:
Why is it that who we are so often becomes determined by our environment?

Before criticizing a person, ask yourself one question: If I had lived in his/her exact life, would I have become any different?

We like to think that people are just "good" or "bad. It simplifies the lives. We praise the successful people for being disciplined, we condemn the criminals for being evil, we admire the kind, and we criticize the angry.We praise successful people because they are disciplined, we condemn the criminals for being evil, we admire the kind and we criticize the angry.

However, life is not so easy.

A child who grows up in a loving, secure, book-rich, inspired home grows up without all the battles that another child has to fight every morning, after waking up to gunshots, domestic violence or no food for the next day. But in society both are supposed to reach the same goal. It's as if you rated two runners the same if they were running a race with one starting 100 metres back.

Your environment teaches you constantly!

People are master adapters.

Let him lie in peace, and he will learn to be patient.

Set them in disorder and they learn to survive.

Provide them with trust and they open up.

Put them in a situation where they are surrounded by betrayal and "all of a sudden 'all look suspicious'.

The paradox is that that which we refer to as personality is sometimes just repeated exposure in familiar attire.

People have always been known to learn behaviors from others. Habits are not inherited – they are downloaded from your surroundings.

Chaos doesn't make character. It Builds Survival.

Spend years constantly wondering if you will have food for the next day. if you are safe in your neighbourhood, if your salary will last another month, and you'll notice how your priorities shift

You won’t plan for 5 years. You consider Friday or even plan just for the next week.

Behavioural economics studies have demonstrated that financial scarcity will reduce the ability to think and act in the long term. The brain is not intended to decrease in intelligence; survival takes up the brain's time.

Peace Is a Luxury Until You've Lived Without It

One is frequently asked, "Why are they so angry all the time?

But a more pertinent question would be, What have they had to endure in order to survive?

The cool, worker in the air-conditioned office who drinks coffee and the street vendor who avoids street harassment before breakfast are in different psychological atmospheres.

To think that both would react exactly the same to the same stimulus as if they were both plants is like expecting a cactus and a rose to flower in the same conditions.

It's not disease that's the most contagious thing, it's behavior.

Happiness spreads.

Fear spreads.

Violence spreads.

Kindness spreads.

The community will tend to mirror the things that they get repeatedly.

If respect is common, people do what people see.

Corruption is commonplace and honesty begins to seem ridiculous.

And perhaps the biggest tragedy in society is that people do not simply adopt culture, they defend it.

But the environment is not an excuse.

So many people get this wrong.

Recognizing environment does NOT equal losing personal responsibility.

People have been able to rise above poverty without compromising their character, and people have had advantages placed in their hands and squandered them all.

Environmental factors help to account for many decisions. Does not justify every decision.

There's one amazing thing about the human spirit,

To choose its own path. To choose differently.

Conclusion

Perhaps we waste too much time asking, What is there wrong with people?

when we should also be asking,But where did they go,where did they live, where did they grow?

For every quiet place of peace, every good school, every caring parent, every honest leader and every act of kindness is quietly forming the next generation of human behavior.

Our surroundings are a creation of ours and almost instantaneously, then, our environment forms us.

And perhaps the highest form of irony is that: We hold people responsible for being products of the world that we are, as a community.

Idowu Olorunjoba  “IJOBA”

500 level, Mechanical Engineering;UNILAG

Great Impact Baptist church Bariga

Gideon 2 Baptist Association

Lagos East Baptist Conference

title: The Giant That Forgot How to Grow
content:
As it is said, it was a giant that forgot how to grow.

The best part of Nigeria's problems is not the lack of resources, it is the lack of direction.

“A country that has all the good things should not be fighting for the basics.”

Nigeria has been dubbed the "Giant of Africa" and that is a tribute to its power, reach, and potential. Nigeria has a population of over 230 million, Huge Oil and Gas Fields, Fertile Agriculture Areas, Abundant Solid Minerals, Growing Youth Population, one of the biggest economies in the continent and should be the leader on the continent in development.

However, for millions of Nigerians, that promise is as of yet a myth, not reality.

“Average citizen” is not the same as that described in the economic reports. Rather, they have to deal with the rise in food prices, the instability of electricity, the decline in their incomes, unemployment, the lack of infrastructure, and an economy that no longer ensures a decent standard of living with hard work.

No one is asking what is going wrong in Nigeria anymore if they were to ask they would know that the question is not actually: Why isn't Nigeria rich?

The question is, Why hasn't Nigeria converted its wealth, into prosperity?

Institutions, not natural resources, are what build nations.

The lesson of the past is not very pleasant. There are countries in the world which have very little natural resource and are very prosperous. Through education, innovation, discipline and good governance, Japan, Singapore and South Korea transformed themselves.

Nigeria, on the other hand, went a different way.

Instead of diversifying its economy, it got dependent on oil. For decades, the country's funds came from crude oil, and agriculture and manufacturing, as well as technology and industrial production, were comparatively neglected.

The result?

An economy susceptible to high oil prices and falling oil prices.An economy that tends to boom and bust on the price of oil, not on its own productivity.

A giant will always have a hard time standing on one foot.

The price of using up without producing.

Go for an urban shopping trip in any of the Nigerian big markets.

Phones imported. Cars imported. Machines imported. Medicine imported.

Products which can be produced locally are still imported.

Each import is a job that was generated somewhere else.

Every factory that fails to remain open forces a greater number of youths into unemployment.

The consumption of an economy can't exceed its production. Then the bill comes in and common folk suffer it through inflation and loss of purchasing power.

The Real Wealth of a Nation Walks on Two Legs

Nigeria has a lot to say about oil.

Maybe they should talk about people more. More than 60% of Nigeria's population is young – a situation which many developed countries would envy.

Youth will become an asset only when they are provided with quality education, employable skills, health and opportunities.

Otherwise a demographic dividend could turn into a demographic burden.

Youth don't just need jobs. They require an economy which can produce them.

Growth is more than GDP

Governments tend to welcome a rise in their gross domestic product (GDP).

However, GDP is not of much consequence to the mother whose food bill has doubled in six months.

To the graduate who's sending out hundreds of job applications with no success, it is a little thing.

To an entrepreneur who spends more on diesel than he does on production, it is of little consequence.

Economic growth should not be measured only by statistics. It should be measured by how ordinary people live.

When growth exists only on paper, it is prosperity without people.

Leadership Is Not Just About Policy!

All administrations have problems to deal with. All governments have tough decisions to make.

However, there is more to it than policies and budgets: Consistency.

Isolated reforms do not make a nation prosperous.

They develop over a long period of time, through vision that transcends the political.

Roads should outlive administrations.

School reform should transcend elections.

Economic policies must be more enduring than campaign slogans.

Development is not a 4-year process! It's a family affair.

The future of Nigeria is yet to be written.

Today's problems are no excuse for pessimism. Nigeria has exceptional entrepreneurs, world-class professionals, groundbreaking technology start-ups, plentiful and productive land, creative industries and resilient citizens who are still building despite the unimaginable challenges.

Crude oil has never been the most important resource of the country.

It is always been their people.

Nigeria can still emerge as the economic giant it has long promised to be, if its institutions are strengthened, its governance is transparent, investments in education and manufacturing are made, its energy becomes more stable and policies give preference to productivity over patronage.

Conclusion

In Nigeria, poverty is not the greatest tragedy. It is potential not made actual.

No country is more fortunate than us and have produced so little in return.

But history has taught us that it is not the crises in which a nation or people find themselves, but the courage with which they face them, that will define a nation.

The future of Nigeria will not depend on the quantity of oil below its surface.

It will be determined by an institutionally strong and effective leadership that sits above it, and the citizens' desire for accountability, innovation, and development across tribal, political, and religious lines.

Giants are not great by their girth.

They make themselves great through the direction that they take their life.

Idowu Olorunjoba  “IJOBA”
